target.title: fix(ai): add handshake timeout to ChatGPT Responses WebSocket connect
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `connectWebSocket()` in the ChatGPT Responses provider
could hang indefinitely when the remote server accepts the TCP connection but
never completes the HTTP WebSocket upgrade.

`connectWebSocket()` uses `globalThis.WebSocket` (standard WebSocket API),
which does **not** support the `ws`-library `handshakeTimeout` option, and the
function had no `setTimeout`-based fallback. When the caller does not set
`options.timeoutMs`, the entire signal chain (buildRequestSignal →
createFirstStreamEventAbortController) has no timeout, and the SSE fallback at
line 374 of `streamOpenAICodexResponses` never triggers because it requires the
WebSocket promise to reject first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a `setTimeout`-based handshake deadline inside `connectWebSocket()`.
The deadline applies unconditionally as a connection-phase timeout:

- **No `options.timeoutMs`**: 30s default (matches Discord/Signal/QQBot)
- **`options.timeoutMs` set**: forwarded as `handshakeTimeoutMs` — the caller's
  explicit budget governs the handshake phase
- **Cancellation-only signal + no `timeoutMs`**: 30s fallback still applies

The timer and the signal's `onAbort` handler race cleanly via the `settled`
flag: whichever fires first settles the promise and `cleanup()` prevents the
other from leaking or double-rejecting.

The effective timeout value is now reflected in the error message instead of
the hardcoded constant.

## User Impact

Users will no longer experience indefinite hangs when the OpenAI ChatGPT
Responses WebSocket server accepts TCP but delays or never completes the HTTP
upgrade. Users who configured a custom `timeoutMs` value will have that budget
respected as the handshake deadline.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests** (new file, 6 tests, all passing):
  - Default 30s timer when no handshakeTimeoutMs
  - Explicit handshakeTimeoutMs (5s) governs the deadline
  - Timer still fires when a cancellation-only signal is present
  - Normal open, error, and abort paths

  ```
  ✓ applies default 30s timer when no handshakeTimeoutMs is specified
  ✓ uses caller-specified handshakeTimeoutMs when provided
  ✓ timer still fires when a cancellation signal is present
  ✓ resolves normally when WebSocket opens before timeout
  ✓ rejects with error when WebSocket errors before timeout
  ✓ rejects with abort error when signal aborts before timeout

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  6 passed (6)
  ```

- **Real-connection proof**: loopback TCP server that accepts connections but
  never sends the HTTP WebSocket upgrade, tested with `handshakeTimeoutMs=5000`
  and **no** external AbortSignal — the built-in timer fires independently:

  ```
  === Handshake timeout proof ===
  Server: TCP accept on :33459, no WebSocket upgrade
  Server: TCP accepted, no WebSocket upgrade
  Duration: 5.043s
  Result: rejected — "WebSocket connection to OpenAI Responses API timed out after 5000ms"
  ```

  The duration (~5.04s) matches the configured 5000ms handshake timeout,
  confirming the timer fires without any external signal or cancellation.

- **Exit path coverage**: All 5 terminal paths (onOpen, onError, onClose,
  onAbort, constructor catch) correctly clear the timer via `cleanup()`. The
  `settled` flag prevents double-rejection if both the timer and an event fire.

- **No regression**: Existing retry tests (5 tests) continue to pass.

- **Test-only export**: `connectWebSocketForTest` exposes the internal function
  for testing only, following the established `parseSSEForTest` pattern.

- **Error message**: now shows the actual effective timeout value (e.g. 5000ms
  when configured, not the hardcoded default constant).

---

AI-assisted.
